payload.question: How many transistors were on the Intel 4004 of 1971, the first commercially available microprocessor?
payload.comparison: The Intel 8086 of 1978, a 16-bit chip, used approximately 20,000 active transistors.

reveal.context: The Intel 4004, released on 15 November 1971, contained 2,300 transistors and ran at a maximum clock rate of 740 to 750 kHz. It was the first microprocessor sold as a component. Seven years later the 8086 used approximately 20,000 active transistors.

sources.excerpt: The Intel 4004 was released by the Intel Corporation on November 15, 1971. It contained 2,300 transistors and had a maximum clock rate of 740 kHz to 750 kHz. The first commercially available (sold as a component) microprocessor was the 4004 from Intel.

The 8086 is a 16-bit microprocessor chip released by Intel on June 8, 1978. The 8086 was implemented using depletion-load nMOS circuitry with approximately 20,000 active transistors (29,000 counting all ROM and PLA sites).
